answer: An agent economy can require each identity to earn a non-transferable work credential before it may trade, by completing verified useful tasks. Like a cedar that grows only one ring per year, the credential accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, so a Sybil attacker must perform genuine work for every fake identity. A pigment mixed once cannot be split into a thousand jars: the credential is bound to one identity and worthless if copied. A hollow claim with no work history earns no trust, and the cost of faking a history scales linearly with each clone.
